Per the Getting Started Guide, sharing an individual file does not grant folder access; recipients see shared items under 'Shared with me'. Least-privilege defaults: users get minimal permissions; admins must explicitly enable elevated ones. The program explicitly invites privilege/role escalation testing — this role ladder is the boundary to test.

The PUT /rest/adminRoles/{id}/users/{user_id} (promote) vs DELETE (demote) endpoints are the privilege-escalation chokepoints. Also /rest/admin/profiles/{id}/users can 'Change user type'.

Admins may allow 'Remember this device' to skip 2FA on trusted devices. Certificate-based authentication and SSO/SAML supported; with LDAP/SSO policies users enter username instead of email. Failed logins can trigger CAPTCHA; lockout thresholds are admin-configurable. Password reset via /rest/users/requestPasswordReset + /rest/users/resetPassword; forced password change endpoint exists.

title: File disclosure access model: 'anyone after authentication' vs 'Recipient Only' (program boundary)
detail: Per the YesWeHack program page itself: for file disclosure to be valid, the file must NOT be marked 'anyone after authentication' — a valid report must bypass 'Recipient Only' or access a file without being authenticated. This confirms two link-visibility tiers exist in the product: broad (any authenticated user) and recipient-restricted. detail: Kiteworks admin/API docs describe two upload paths. Simple: POST /rest/folders/{id}/actions/file as multipart MIME; the new file's ID is returned in the X-Accellion-Location response header. Large/chunked: POST /folders/{id}/actions/initiateUpload (new file) or POST /files/{file_id}/actions/initiateUpload (new version); required param is file name, optional totalSize/totalChunks, with a lastChunk flag on the final block. Uploading a file whose name already exists in the folder creates a NEW VERSION of that file rather than rejecting or renaming.
evidence: Kiteworks admin guide (API section): 'To add a file to a folder, we need to use the POST end point /rest/folders/{id}/actions/file... the id specified in the X-Accellion-Location field... Chunk Upload Process Steps... POST /folders/{id}/actions/initiateUpload... If you call POST /folders/{id}/actions/initiateUpload with the file name already exists in this folder, a new version of this file will be created.'

title: AV/DLP/ATP/CDR pipeline is ICAP-integrated with per-file encryption
detail: Security architecture white paper: AV servers can be configured as a dedicated cluster role to scan client files for malware. DLP via ICAP (e.g. Forcepoint, Digital Guardian) scans OUTBOUND data with alert/log/block policies. ATP via ICAP (Check Point SandBlast, Trellix) quarantines failing inbound files. CDR (Forcepoint Zero Trust CDR) sanitizes each inbound document and Kiteworks forwards the SANITIZED version to the recipient, not the original. Every file is individually encrypted with a unique AES-256-CTR key, plus FIPS 140-2 disk encryption; TLS in transit. NOTE: program accepts AV bypass-by-rename as known risk - do not report that class.
evidence: Kiteworks Security White Paper (kiteworks.com): 'Antivirus (AV)/Data Loss Prevention (DLP) - Kiteworks enables you to configure antivirus servers in your cluster that can be set up as a dedicated role to scan client files for malware'; 'each file is individually encrypted with a unique key using FIPS 140-2 approved AES-256-CTR'. Advanced Governance brief: CDR 'immediately returns a sanitized, usable version of the document that Kiteworks forwards to the recipient'; DLP 'can alert, log, and/or block transfers based on the DLP results'.

title: Size limits are policy-configurable, not technical: no per-file limit, 100GB folder uploads, up to 16TB licensed
detail: SEC external user guide: 'There is no size limit on files. There is a 100 GB limit per folder upload.' Kiteworks licensing doc: 'Large File Sizes - Transfer files up to 16 TB in size.' CPUC external guide: external users can send folders with combined size of 500MB. Upload path also supports 'Upload Local Folders'. Implication: size enforcement lives in policy config, and very large uploads (chunked) are a designed, supported flow - worth noting for the human operator's manual tests (e.g. chunked-upload edge cases, timeout/partial-upload states).
evidence: sec.gov Kiteworks guide: 'Click on Add Files, and select Upload Local Files or Upload Local Folders. There is no size limit on files. There is a 100 GB limit per folder upload.' Kiteworks Enterprise 8.0 Packaging/Licensing: 'Transfer files up to 16 TB in size.'

title: Share/send flow and data-lifecycle asymmetry
detail: Documented user flow: compose message -> add recipients (To/Cc/Bcc, comma/semicolon separated) -> Add Files (upload local files or folders) -> Send -> recipient gets email notification with attachment link -> recipient must authenticate -> download. Notable lifecycle facts: (1) received files expire - 'You will have 30 days after receipt of the message to download the files before they are removed from your Kiteworks mailbox' (SEC deployment); (2) 'If you delete a sent message, it will not delete the message for the recipient' - sender-side deletion does not revoke recipient access, a data-lifecycle asymmetry relevant to business-logic review.
evidence: sec.gov Kiteworks guide: 'Receiving Files: ... You can start the download by clicking on the Attachment link within the email. You will be asked to authenticate... Note: You will have 30 days after receipt of the message to download the files before they are removed from your Kiteworks mailbox... If you delete a sent message, it will not delete the message for the recipient.'

title: Historical CVEs in this exact pipeline: pre-9.2.0 arbitrary upload, SDF unrestricted dangerous-type upload, Core access-control
detail: OpenCVE records for Kiteworks: (1) Prior to 9.2.0, a configuration vulnerability allowed uploading of arbitrary files WITHOUT proper validation - malicious admins could upload unauthorized file types. (2) CVE-2026-23636: Secure Data Forms prior to 9.2.1 - a form MANAGER could exploit 'Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type' due to missing validation. (3) CVE-2026-23514 (CVSS 8.8): Kiteworks Core 9.2.0/9.2.1 access-control flaw letting authenticated users access unauthorized content (patched 9.2.2). (4) CVE-2026-24750: SDF stored XSS when modifying forms (patched 9.2.1). These show the upload-validation and file-access-authorization seams have been the historically buggy surface - the human operator should prioritize upload validation bypass (non-rename vectors), version-overwrite authorization, and IDOR on file objects in the manual phase.
evidence: app.opencve.io Kiteworks listing: 'Prior to version 9.2.0, a vulnerability in Kiteworks configuration allows uploading of arbitrary files without proper validation'; CVE-2026-23636 'the manager of a form could potentially exploit an Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type due to a missing validation'; CVE-2026-23514 'Versions 9.2.0 and 9.2.1 of Kiteworks Core have an access control vulnerability that allows authenticated users to access unauthorized content.'

title: AHEP module governs sends at compose time - new logic surface
detail: Kiteworks launched Agent and Human Error Prevention (AHEP), a module of the Data Policy Engine that analyzes signals AS a message is composed: recipient type, recipient volume, identity match, attachment presence, domain validity. Pre-built policies: BCC/reply-all protection, send-to-self detection (fires on personal-domain recipient + identity match + attachment). This is a new policy-enforcement layer sitting in front of the send/share pipeline - its bypass or misconfiguration is a fresh business-logic surface (e.g. can the warnings be suppressed, do they apply to API-driven sends, do they cover MFT transfers or only email compose).
evidence: Kiteworks press release (Aug 2026): 'AHEP analyzes multiple signals simultaneously as a message is composed: recipient type, recipient volume, identity match, attachment presence, and domain validity... BCC/reply-all protection flags exposure... Send-to-self detection fires only when a personal-domain recipient, a close identity match to the sender across four independent dimensions, and an attachment all align.'

title: Intended file flow, end to end (for the human operator's mental model)
detail: Upload: user selects local files/folders (any size; folder uploads capped per policy, e.g. 100GB) -> multipart or chunked-upload session (initiateUpload, file name + totalSize/totalChunks or lastChunk) -> server-side AV/ATP/CDR scanning via ICAP integrations (inbound docs may be CDR-sanitized and REPLACED before delivery) -> per-file AES-256-CTR encryption at rest. Share: compose -> recipients + subject -> Send -> policy engine checks (DLP outbound scan: alert/log/block; AHEP misdirected-send warnings) -> recipient notified by email -> recipient authenticates -> downloads via attachment link. Lifecycle: 30-day mailbox expiry on received files; sender deletion does NOT revoke recipient copies. Same-name re-upload creates a new file VERSION.
evidence: Synthesized from Kiteworks Security White Paper, admin/API guide, SEC external user guide, Advanced Governance brief, and AHEP launch material cited in observations above.

title: Kiteworks Core supports Active Directory (LDAP) auth with admin-configured directory parameters
detail: Official Kiteworks installation/deployment prerequisite checklist lists authentication types: Active Directory (LDAP), Single Sign-On, Self Registration, Manual Account Entry. LDAP setup fields: IP/hostname of domain controller, Protocol, Port, Base DN, Bind DN. Two-factor options: Radius or built-in email OTP, with a dedicated 'LDAP Username Attribute' field tying OTP/auth to a directory attribute.
evidence: kiteworks.com deployment prerequisite PDF (Checklist - Installation and Deployment Prerequisite), items 11/11a/11c

title: LDAP attributes drive automatic provisioning and profile/role assignment
detail: Kiteworks NYDFS brief states LDAP/AD integration enables automatic user onboarding, offboarding, and role updates 'with flexible profile assignments based on LDAP attributes'. Trust boundary: directory attribute values map to Kiteworks profiles/privileges — whoever controls directory attributes influences authorization.
evidence: kiteworks.com kiteworks-brief-ny-financial-cyber.pdf: 'flexible profile assignments based on LDAP attributes'

title: REST API exposes /ldapGroups endpoints; LDAP groups usable for end-user folder sharing
detail: Admin guide documents /ldapGroups/ API endpoints: admins can make LDAP groups available to end users when sharing folders; apps can add/update/remove LDAP groups exposed to users. Interactive API reference at <install>/rest/index.html#!/ldapGroups. Group names flow from API input toward directory queries.
evidence: Kiteworks admin guide (mirror): 'If your settings are integrated with LDAP, administrators can allow LDAP groups to be available to end users when sharing folders... using /ldapGroups/endpoints'

title: SAML 2.0 SP appears to be SimpleSAMLphp-based
detail: Microsoft Entra SSO tutorial gives Kiteworks ACS URL pattern https://<kiteworksURL>/sp/module.php/saml/sp/saml2-acs.php/sp-sso. The module.php/saml/sp/saml2-acs.php path is SimpleSAMLphp's canonical SAML SP endpoint. If accurate, the SAML SP stack inherits SimpleSAMLphp's known vulnerability history (signature handling, XML parsing).
evidence: learn.microsoft.com Entra Kiteworks SAML tutorial, Basic SAML Configuration Identifier pattern

title: SSO Setup exposes security-relevant toggles: SP Entity ID, signed AuthnRequests, IP-range auto-redirect
detail: Admin path: Applications > Authentication and Authorization > SSO Setup. Settings include: Initiate AuthnRequest checkbox, IdP Entity ID, Service Provider Entity ID (Oracle docs show default value https://kiteworks.com — a shared/fixed SP entity ID across tenants), SSO Service URL, Sign AuthnRequest checkbox, RSA public key certificate paste. Deployment checklist adds 'Auto Redirect IP or Range' forcing SSO by source IP.
evidence: docs.oracle.com Oracle IDCS Kiteworks SSO guide; manageengine Kiteworks SAML guide; kiteworks.com deployment checklist item 11b

title: IdP-assigned users may get access without a pre-existing Kiteworks account
detail: Oracle IDCS guide notes: 'The kiteworks app can be accessed by a user who is assigned to the kiteworks app in Oracle Identity Cloud Service, even if the user does not have a kiteworks account.' Implies just-in-time provisioning driven by IdP assertion attributes — trust boundary: IdP-supplied attributes create/authorize accounts.
evidence: docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/paas/identity-cloud/idcsc/kiteworks.html

title: EPG Data Policy Engine sits in the mail stream and acts on parsed message attributes
detail: Email Protection Gateway automatically enforces policy on every inbound and outbound message. Data Policy Engine decides encrypt/route/quarantine/reject based on sender, recipient, data content, classification label, and message attributes — 60+ actions over 50+ conditions. Inbound mail from arbitrary external senders is untrusted input into this parser/policy engine.
evidence: kiteworks.com/platform/simple/email-protection-gateway/

title: EPG trusts client-applied MIP sensitivity labels and parses S/MIME, OpenPGP, DKIM/DMARC
detail: EPG consumes Microsoft MIP sensitivity labels in policy rules, supports S/MIME and OpenPGP, DMARC via DKIM, signed email via certificates, integrated PKI with public CAs, customer-controlled rotation of internal server keys, automated key management. Trust boundaries: label values asserted by senders, certificate/PKI validation, encrypted-attachment handling crossing EPG into Core storage.
evidence: kiteworks.com EPG feature briefs (2022-2023) and EPG glossary page

title: Email-triggered file flows bridge EPG and Core: large attachments up to 16TB via Outlook plugin/web
detail: EPG use cases include large attachments (up to 16 TB) sent via Outlook plugin or web, scanned with DLP/AV/ATP. Attachment upload path crosses the email boundary into Kiteworks storage — file-processing attack surface reachable via crafted email attachments.
evidence: kiteworks.com EPG feature brief: 'Large attachments up to 16 TB (via web and Outlook Plugin)'; 'Scan files with DLP, antivirus (AV), and advanced threat prevention (ATP)'

title: LDAP injection input-flow map: login username, admin filters, group names, attribute values
detail: Candidate LDAP filter-construction points from docs: (1) login username matched against directory attributes (uid/sAMAccountName/mail pattern per deployment checklist + ownCloud-family LDAP login-filter design); (2) admin-configured Base DN / search filters / username attribute; (3) /ldapGroups API group-name input; (4) LDAP attribute values mapped to profiles/roles (attribute-controlled authorization); (5) 'LDAP Username Attribute' in 2FA config. Program explicitly wants LDAP injection — these are the flows to test manually.
evidence: Synthesis of observations above; kiteworks.com deployment checklist; admin guide /ldapGroups; NYDFS brief

title: Search operations inventory: name + content search, tenant-wide
detail: Kiteworks exposes search/search_folders/search_files (official kiteworks/mcp repo, mirrors REST API): search by name for folders/files, search_files also by document content. Usage examples show tenant-wide queries ('find all files matching Q1 across Kiteworks'). Search requires the Search READ scope. Full-text search covers file/folder names AND text within documents.
evidence: https://github.com/kiteworks/mcp/blob/HEAD/docs/AVAILABLE_TOOLS.md (Search Operations section); https://github.com/kiteworks/mcp/blob/HEAD/docs/USAGE_EXAMPLES.md (Ex.1-3)

title: Full-text search spans connected external repositories
detail: Kiteworks docs: the search engine 'runs a search across the file/folder names and the text within a document regardless of the storage location of the file: inside the Kiteworks native repository, or in connected SharePoint systems and file shares.' Search therefore crosses the trust boundary between Kiteworks and externally-connected repositories with their own ACLs.
evidence: https://www.kiteworks.com/sites/default/files/resources/kiteworks-sample-rfp-content-firewall-accellion.pdf (Full Text Search capability)

title: No server-side owner/creator filter; ownership filtered client-side
detail: Empirically confirmed against the live API (kiteworks/claude-agent-marketplace): there is NO server-side 'owner' or 'creator' filter on search/search_files/search_folders. Consumers walk get_folder_children and filter client-side on each item's creator/userId field. Every search result carries creator/userId metadata visible to the searcher — the authorization boundary is 'what objects are returned', not 'what metadata is shown'.
evidence: https://github.com/kiteworks/claude-agent-marketplace/blob/HEAD/offboarding-content-finder/skills/offboarding-content-finder-preview/SKILL.md

title: Search behavioral boundaries: text term required, recursive with parent scope
detail: Tested behavior: unscoped queries and parent_folder_id + date-filter-only queries (no text term) return 'No results found'. parent_folder_id + text term IS recursive into subfolders (2+ levels). content_contains requires a folder scope and cannot be used tenant-wide. So name search is tenant-wide; content search is folder-scoped.
evidence: https://github.com/kiteworks/claude-agent-marketplace/blob/HEAD/redactor/skills/folder-scan/SKILL.md

title: Mail listing filters: bucket, status, read state, sender, shared mailbox
detail: list_mail supports filters (bucket, status, read state, sender, shared mailbox) + pagination. get_mail returns subject, body, AV/DLP scan status, recipients, attachments. The 'shared mailbox' filter is the interesting boundary: it selects across mailboxes, so its authorization check determines whether a user can enumerate mailboxes they are not a member of.
evidence: https://github.com/kiteworks/mcp/blob/HEAD/docs/AVAILABLE_TOOLS.md (Mail section)

title: User/LDAP search surfaces: exact-email lookup and LDAP/AD search
detail: find_user_by_email: exact email -> display name + UUID. search_users_ldap: searches the configured LDAP/Active Directory by email or display name (Users READ scope). Admin API adds search_users with optional filters + pagination, list_user_profiles, list_profile_users with filters. The LDAP search takes free-text display-name/email input into an LDAP/AD query.
evidence: https://github.com/kiteworks/mcp/blob/HEAD/docs/AVAILABLE_TOOLS.md (User Operations, Admin sections)

title: Admin search surfaces: activity logs with free-text search and filters
detail: get_user_activity / get_admin_activity: date range + free-text search + activity-type/event/object filters + pagination. list_mailboxes: shared mailboxes with filters + pagination. Admin-scoped, so lower priority for a non-admin researcher, but the filter parameters are attacker-influenced input into log queries.
evidence: https://github.com/kiteworks/mcp/blob/HEAD/docs/AVAILABLE_TOOLS.md (Admin sections)

title: Intended search boundary: need-to-know / granular access controls
detail: Docs state VDRs 'expose virtual data room files and folders only to parties with a need to know' while offering 'find any data with full-text search'. Intended invariant: search results must never include objects the searcher has no access to, including via connected repositories. Any deviation (search returning unshared objects, creator metadata on objects outside access, shared-mailbox filter crossing membership) violates the stated model.
evidence: https://www.kiteworks.com/platform/simple/virtual-data-rooms/?hsLang=en

title: H1: LDAP search input may allow LDAP filter injection (program explicitly wants LDAPi)
detail: search_users_ldap takes user-influenced email/display-name text into an LDAP/AD query. If the input is concatenated into an LDAP filter without escaping, classic LDAP injection (e.g. *)(uid=*))(|(uid=*) style probes) could alter query semantics. The program explicitly lists LDAP injection as a focus area. Manual test for the operator: benign metacharacter probes (*, parens) in the LDAP search field observing result-set anomalies vs. baseline.
evidence: Tool exists per official MCP docs; injection untested (no access). Program focus area per YesWeHack policy.

title: H2: content/full-text search may not respect connected-repository ACLs
detail: Since search indexes SharePoint/file-share content 'regardless of storage location', a mismatch between Kiteworks-side result filtering and the external repository's ACLs could surface snippets or metadata of files the searcher cannot open. Manual test for the operator: two accounts with different external-share access run identical content searches and diff result sets.
evidence: Docs claim cross-repository search; ACL enforcement at search time is undocumented.

title: Share-access tiers are explicitly named: 'Recipient Only' vs 'anyone after authentication'
detail: YesWeHack Kiteworks program page defines the file-disclosure bar in the product's own terms: a report is valid only if it bypasses 'Recipient Only' or accesses a file without being authenticated; files marked 'anyone after authentication' are accepted risk. So the product exposes at least two named share-access tiers: (1) Recipient Only — restricted to the named recipient(s); (2) anyone-after-authentication — any authenticated user may access.
evidence: https://yeswehack.com/programs/kiteworks-public-bug-bounty-program-1 — Known Issues/Accepted risks: 'For file disclosure, ensure that the file is not marked as "anyone after authentication". To be valid you must be able to bypass "Recipient Only" or accessing a file without being authenticated.'

title: Secure-link token model: double 128-bit MD5 token; qualified links carry admin-configurable lifespan
detail: Accellion/Kiteworks Security FAQ documents the link model: SECURE LINK/URL generated by a double 128-bit MD5 token (2^128 combinations, unguessable); QUALIFIED LINK/URL adds a limited lifespan configurable by the System Administrator, blocking access after expiration.
evidence: https://www.kiteworks.com/sites/default/files/resources/accellionsecurityfaq.pdf — AUTHENTICATION section: 'SECURE LINK/URL: Generated by a double 128-bit MD5 token'; 'QUALIFIED LINK/URL: The link has a limited lifespan (configurable by the System Administrator to conform to company policy) and blocks access to the file after its expiration.'

title: Challenge/response + recipient validation: pre-download identity check, anti-forwarding, admin-configurable
detail: Before download, CHALLENGE/RESPONSE requires users to identify themselves (linked to customer LDAP when deployed). RECIPIENT VALIDATION verifies the downloader is on the original recipient list, which prevents forwarded links from working. Both are System Administrator configurable options — i.e., they can be OFF depending on deployment.
evidence: accellionsecurityfaq.pdf: 'CHALLENGE/RESPONSE: Before download, the users must identify themselves. When LDAP is deployed, Accellion will link this feature to the customer's LDAP directories.' / 'RECIPIENT VALIDATION: Accellion can verify if a user is on the original recipient list of the email for downloading a file. This prevents forwarding links. This is a System Administrators configurable option.'

title: Per-send sender controls: who may download, link duration, download count, recipient-unique watermarks
detail: When emailing files, senders can specify whether the recipient must authenticate before downloading, control who can download via the secure link, how long the link works, and how many downloads it allows. Files carry a per-recipient unique watermark by default; the email body itself can also be secured behind authentication.
evidence: https://www.kiteworks.com/sites/default/files/resources/wp-kiteworks-security-overview_.pdf — 'When emailing files from kiteworks, endusers can apply security settings to specify whether the recipient must authenticate his/her identity before downloading the file' / 'endusers can control who can download the file via the secure link, how long the secure link will work, and how many downloads the secure link will allow' / watermarks unique to the file recipient by default.

title: Folder role ladder: Viewer / Uploader / Downloader / Collaborator / Manager / Owner with exact capability splits
detail: Viewer: view but cannot download. Uploader: upload and manage own files, cannot see others' files. Downloader: view/download, cannot upload or assign tasks. Collaborator: full file access, cannot manage others' access. Manager: full access + create/delete nested folders + control others' access. Owner: highest control, owns storage quota, default = folder creator. Admins decide which roles end users may assign.
evidence: https://www.kiteworks.com/sites/default/files/resources/kiteworks-sample-rfp-content-firewall-accellion.pdf p.18 (Company and Product Overview): role definitions verbatim; 'Recipient Identity Verification: Kiteworks file access requires users to authenticate, with certain exceptions that must be enabled by the administrator and user'; 'File Access Expiration: File and folder expirations are native properties which can be configured by both users and administrators.'

title: Expiry/deletion model: expired send-links delete files from server; mailbox retention ~30 days
detail: Files sent via Kiteworks upload to the server and a link goes to recipients; after the link expires the files are deleted from the server. Recipients without an account are prompted to create one. SEC deployment guide: recipients have 30 days after receipt to download before files are removed from the mailbox.
evidence: https://global.mftservice.com/sw/guide/Kiteworks_Getting_Started_Guide.pdf p.15 ('After the link expires, the files are deleted from the server. If a recipient doesn't have a user account on the server, they'll be prompted to create one.'); https://www.sec.gov/files/kiteworksguide_0.pdf ('You will have 30 days after receipt of the message to download the files before they are removed from your Kiteworks mailbox.')

title: Recipient onboarding flow ('Access Message'): same-email check + self-registration + email activation
detail: External recipient flow: click 'Access Message' in email -> enter the SAME email address the message was sent to -> if unregistered, set a password and create an account -> activation email -> activate -> inbox with download link. Identity proof is: control of the recipient email inbox. No out-of-band identity verification in the default flow.
evidence: https://ocg.nsw.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-02/G_SOOHC_KiteworksUserGuide.pdf ('Enter your email address (this must be the same email address that the above email was sent to)... If you have not already registered this email address you will be prompted to set a password... click the Activate Account button'); consistent with sec.gov guide ('You will be asked to authenticate').

title: Recipient tracking/audit: recipient email, access time, IP logged per download
detail: RECIPIENT TRACKING logs the recipient email address, time of access, and IP address for downloads, intended to make suspicious access monitorable. Combined with per-recipient watermarks, the product's anti-leak story leans on attribution rather than only prevention.
evidence: accellionsecurityfaq.pdf: 'RECIPIENT TRACKING: Logging of Recipient email address, time of access and IP address makes it easy to monitor suspicious activity.'

title: Handoff: the testable seam is 'Recipient Only' enforcement, not the tier labels
detail: FOR THE HUMAN OPERATOR (not a finding): the program draws the validity line at bypassing 'Recipient Only' or reaching a file unauthenticated. Given recipient validation is an admin-configurable OPTION and self-registration lets any email-holder become 'authenticated', the seams worth manual testing are: (a) whether recipient validation is actually enforced on the hunting env's download endpoints for Recipient-Only shares (e.g., token replay from a different authenticated identity); (b) whether expiry/download-count limits are enforced server-side vs client-side; (c) whether role checks (Viewer cannot download) hold on direct /rest/files/{id}/content access. Do NOT test 'anyone after authentication' disclosure — accepted risk.
evidence: Tier definitions from yeswehack.com program page; enforcement optionality from accellionsecurityfaq.pdf ('This is a System Administrators configurable option'); role capability splits from RFP doc. No live testing performed — docs analysis only.

title: Two-tier authorization model: system admin roles vs per-folder user roles
detail: Kiteworks separates authorization into two independent tiers. Tier 1: system-level admin roles (System Administrator, Application Administrator, Helpdesk Administrator, DLI/data-leak investigator, plus Compliance Administrator, CISO Administrator, security analytics admins, MFT admins per compliance docs). Tier 2: per-folder/per-file end-user roles (Owner, Manager, Collaborator, Downloader, Uploader, Viewer). The tiers are independently assignable; holding a high folder role confers zero admin capability and vice versa.
evidence: kiteworks.com insider-threats page: 'System Administrator, Compliance Administrator, CISO Administrator — independently assignable, non-self-escalating'; PCI DSS guide lists folder roles Owner/Manager/Collaborator/Downloader/Viewer/Uploader; NIST CSF 2.0 guide: 'four default admin roles (System, Application, Helpdesk, and DLI) and allows creation of custom roles by copying and modifying existing roles'

title: Anti-escalation invariant: users cannot self-promote; only System Admins assign admin roles
detail: The documented invariant is explicit: only system administrators can designate users as administrators (including application administrators); users cannot promote themselves to system administrators. The /adminRoles REST API requires authentication as an administrative user. Custom admin roles are created by copying existing ones, with each permission set to no-access / view-only / full-access. This is the single most valuable invariant to test: any path that lets a non-system-admin grant admin roles, or a user elevate their own admin role, breaks the designed model.
evidence: Admin guide (weebly PDF of Kiteworks admin guide): 'NOTE: To use adminRoles API your application will need to authenticate with administrative users. In addition, only system administrators can [designate] users to administer the system, application administrators. Users cannot promote themselves to system administrators.'

title: Folder role permission matrix: Viewer < Downloader < Uploader < Collaborator < Manager < Owner
detail: Per-folder RBAC ladder (from Kiteworks mobile app user guide, Appendix A): Viewer can view files/activity/users only. Downloader adds download, comments, notifications, task assignment. Collaborator adds upload, edit, version view/promote/delete, lock/unlock, task assignment to others. Manager adds user/role management within the folder. Owner has all. Uploader is upload-only. When sharing, the sharer's admin determines which roles they may grant — role-granting itself is a privilege, not a right.
evidence: archive.org Kiteworks Mobile App User's Guide Appendix A 'User Roles and Access Privileges' table; Getting Started Guide: 'When you share a file, you can assign users the Collaborator role... or the Viewer role... Your Kiteworks administrator determines which roles you can assign.'

title: Least-privilege defaults with deny-by-default; elevation requires explicit admin action
detail: Kiteworks is designed so users automatically receive the least permissions necessary; administrators must explicitly enable elevated permissions. The access-control system defaults to deny-all: access is granted only when explicitly authorized. For hunting, this means the interesting failures are grants that appear without explicit admin action, or defaults that are more permissive than documented (e.g., a share defaulting to Collaborator instead of Viewer).
evidence: kiteworks.com CISA secure-by-design guide: 'users are automatically given the least permissions necessary; administrators must explicitly enable elevated permissions'; PCI DSS guide: access control system 'set to deny all by default'.

title: ABAC layer: action privilege does NOT confer content access (attribute-based restriction)
detail: On top of RBAC, Kiteworks applies attribute-based access control: ABAC policies restrict admin content access based on classification — holding an action privilege does not grant access to the content itself. The Data Policy Engine combines RBAC+ABAC. This is a second designed invariant: an administrator with permission to perform an action (e.g., manage a folder) should still be denied the file content if ABAC classification forbids it. Test target: operations where the ABAC check is skipped but the RBAC check passes.
evidence: kiteworks.com insider-threats page: 'Attribute-based content restriction | ABAC policies restrict admin content access based on classification — action privilege does not confer content access'; Defence Standard 05-138 guide: 'Data Policy Engine combines Kiteworks data access controls including ABAC and RBAC controls'.

title: Separation of duties: admins are walled off from end-user data and the OS
detail: Administrators are separated from end users and subdivided (system, application, help desk, security analytics, data leak investigators, MFT admins). Administrators cannot log into the operating system or access data directly. Vendor support access is customer-initiated, time-bounded, and requires two-party (4-eyes) authorization before a session opens. All administrative operations are audit-logged (632-event catalogue, tamper-evident, syslog-exportable). Hunting implication: any admin function reachable by a non-admin identity, or any data access by an admin outside their ABAC scope, is a boundary violation.
evidence: kiteworks.com company/product overview: 'Separation of Duties: Administrators are separated from end users... Administrators can't log into the operating system or access data.'; insider-threats page: dual authorization for vendor support, 632-event audit catalogue.

title: External vs internal user boundary: licensed vs non-licensed external users
detail: User population is split: Internal Users vs External Users. External users are further split into Licensed (Collaborator/Manager/Owner folder roles, or can initiate email) and Non-licensed (Viewer/Downloader/Uploader only). Notably: an external user who can both upload AND download to the same folder counts as Licensed. This licensing boundary is itself an authorization-relevant state transition — a non-licensed external user gaining edit/manage capability crosses into licensed territory, which the system is supposed to track and charge for.
evidence: kiteworks.com Packaging and Licensing doc (Enterprise 8.0): 'External Users: All other users... Licensed Users: ... privileges to at least edit, download, upload, and manage all files in at least one folder (Collaborator, Manager, and Owner folder roles)... Nonlicensed Users: External Users who can only view, download, or upload. If an External User can upload and download to the same folder, they are considered a Licensed User.'

title: Privilege-management API surface: /profiles, /roles, /adminRoles, /ldapGroups
detail: The REST API exposes privilege-management endpoints: /profiles (manage privileges/features assigned to users), /roles (directory roles), /adminRoles (assign administrator roles — admin auth required), /ldapGroups (manage LDAP groups available to end users for sharing). These are the programmatic enforcement points of the authorization model. Per design, /adminRoles and privilege-mutating /profiles calls must reject non-admin callers; any such call succeeding with a low-privilege token is a vertical escalation.
evidence: Kiteworks admin guide (API reference section): '/profiles/ endpoint... manage the privileges assigned to kiteworks users'; 'adminRoles API allows your application to manage the assignment of administrator roles to users. NOTE: To use adminRoles API your application will need to authenticate with administrative users.'

title: Ranked privilege boundaries for hypothesis generation (where escalation pays)
detail: Boundaries ordered by bounty value and likelihood of implementation flaw: (1) non-admin -> any admin role via /adminRoles or /profiles (vertical, program-explicit focus); (2) folder-role ladder jumps, especially Viewer->Downloader (download of 'view-only' files) and Collaborator->Manager (user/role management); (3) action-privilege -> content access bypassing ABAC classification; (4) external non-licensed -> licensed capabilities without license state change; (5) share-link recipient -> owner/manager of the shared object; (6) helpdesk/admin scoped role -> system admin scope. LDAP-integrated environments add: LDAP group membership -> Kiteworks role mapping errors.
evidence: Synthesis of observations 1-8 above; program focus areas: 'horizontal and vertical privilege escalation' qualifying; LDAP injection explicitly in focus.

title: User entity has distinct lifecycle flags: active/suspended/deactivated/deleted/verified
detail: Admin-guide user JSON shows separate booleans: active, suspended, deactivated, deleted, verified, plus internal (bool), userTypeId (int), flag. Deprovisioning is therefore a multi-state pipeline (suspend -> deactivate -> delete), not a single delete. /users/me returns status (active, deleted).
evidence: watoniworawi.weebly.com admin-guide PDF user JSON: {active:true, deactivated:false, deleted:false, suspended:false, verified:true, internal:true, userTypeId:1, syncdirId:5, mydirId:4, basedirId:3}; kiteworks.com API guide: /users/me returns status (active, deleted)

title: Every user gets an auto-created 'My Folder' (syncdirId) at provisioning
detail: /rest/users/me returns syncdirId = auto-created default 'My Folder' plus mydirId/basedirId. Identity creation is coupled to folder-tree creation: a new identity always owns a root folder object.
evidence: kiteworks.com/sites/default/api/ : 'One of the attributes returned was syncdirId, which refers to your automatically created default My Folder'

title: Self-provisioning on share invite: recipient creates account with matching email
detail: When a file/mail is sent to an address with no account, the recipient is prompted to create one. The email entered MUST match the invited address (SEC guide). Optional sender-issued activation code (out-of-band identity check), CAPTCHA, email verification link, optional mobile OTP. No open self-registration without an invite trigger.
evidence: Kiteworks Getting Started Guide p.5 (global.mftservice.com/sw/guide): 9-step create-account flow; sec.gov kiteworksguide: 'You must enter the same email address that you originally received the invite from'; Qlarant end-user instructions: invite -> create password -> welcome email -> email passcode 2FA

title: External invitees default to 'restricted user' with time-bounded validity
detail: SEC deployment: new external users are configured as restricted users by default; account enables send/receive for 120 days to that staff member. So the identity model includes a restricted/external user class with expiry — deprovisioning can be time-driven, not just admin-driven.
evidence: sec.gov/files/kiteworksguide_0.pdf: 'by default you will be configured as a restricted user... for 120 days'

title: Privileges are assigned via User Profiles; folder access via folder roles; admin power via admin roles
detail: Three-layer model: (1) User Profiles (/profiles/) = feature/privilege bundles per user; (2) folder roles (/roles/) = Collaborator (edit/download/send) vs Viewer, admin decides assignable roles; (3) adminRoles = System Administrator / Application Administrator. Only System Admin can promote to System/Application Admin; users cannot self-promote. Admin user CRUD via /admin (list/add/update/delete users, settings, admin roles, profile image).
evidence: kiteworks.com/sites/default/api/ Security APIs section: profiles, roles, adminRoles, admin endpoints

title: SSO supports SP-initiated login with Just-In-Time provisioning; LDAP groups can be exposed to end users
detail: Entra ID integration: SP-initiated SSO + JIT user provisioning (accounts auto-created on first SSO login). LDAP-integrated installs let admins expose LDAP groups to end users for folder sharing; /ldapGroups/ API manages them. So identities can originate from IdP/LDAP, not just local creation.
evidence: learn.microsoft.com Entra Kiteworks tutorial: 'Kiteworks supports SP initiated SSO... Just In Time user provisioning'; API guide: LDAP Groups section

title: Identity extends to devices and external content sources
detail: Per-user device tracking with remote wipe (/devices/, /admin/devices/). Enterprise Connect sources let users link external repositories (SharePoint, Documentum) to their identity. A user identity is therefore a hub: folders + devices + external sources + contacts/groups.
evidence: kiteworks.com/sites/default/api/: devices section; sources section; admin devices endpoints

title: Contacts and personal groups are identity-adjacent sharing primitives
detail: Users manage contacts (/contacts/) and define personal contact groups (/groups/) used for folder access grants and mail. Groups are user-created, distinct from LDAP groups. Sharing can target users, personal groups, or LDAP groups.
evidence: kiteworks.com/sites/default/api/: contacts, groups, LDAP Groups sections

title: Folder role hierarchy: Owner > Manager > Collaborator > Viewer
detail: Kiteworks secure folders use a four-tier role model. Owners and Managers can manage users/stakeholders and assign roles, set folders as Restricted, and share via secure links. Collaborators can edit via web/mobile editors but in Restricted folders cannot download. Viewers get browser/mobile online viewing without download rights. Ownership is thus a distinct, named role on folders, not just 'creator'.
evidence: kiteworks.com security overview PDF (wp-kiteworks-security-overview_): 'Folder Owners, Managers, and Collaborators can share files securely'; 'Folder Owners and Managers can manage users and internal and external stakeholders... by assigning them user roles'; 'Viewers can view documents within the browser or Mobile App without being granted permission to download'

title: File-level sharing is independent of folder access; Collaborator role includes 'send'
detail: Individual files can be shared without granting access to the rest of the folder; recipients see them under 'Shared with me'. The Collaborator role grants edit, download, SEND the file, and more; Viewer is limited. The admin determines which roles a user may assign. The 'send' permission on Collaborator implies a collaborator can re-distribute the file (a delegation chain), which is the key re-share question for hypothesis agents.
evidence: Kiteworks Getting Started Guide (kiteworks.sauder.com PDF p.14): 'You can share individual files in a folder without giving users access to other files in the folder... assign users the Collaborator role with permissions to edit, download, send the file, and more. Or... the Viewer role... Your Kiteworks administrator determines which roles you can assign.'

title: User deletion: 'Delete All Folders Owned by the User and All Files Sent to Others' + reassignment wizard
detail: Kiteworks user profiles historically had a 'Deleted Inactive Account' setting with option 'Delete All Folders Owned by the User and All Files Sent to Others' (converted in 7.7 to 'Delete Account When Deactivated'). To free a license while retaining data, an admin deletes the inactive user manually and a wizard guides reassignment of their data to a licensed user. So ownership has an explicit, admin-driven transfer path ONLY at deletion time; deactivation alone retains the data under the inactive account (license still consumed).
evidence: kiteworks.com User License Recycling Update brief (Feature-Brief_User-License-Recycling-Update-7.7_FINAL_220210.pdf): 'the wizard will guide you to reassign their data to a licensed user as part of the process'; 'Delete All Folders Owned by the User and All Files Sent to Others'

title: Deactivation preserves data and (historically) sessions; sole active admin is protected
detail: Deactivating a user removes access but the account still holds data (license not freed until data reassigned/deleted). A user who is the sole active admin cannot be deactivated, and a user assigned to scheduled jobs cannot be deactivated — an ownership-safety invariant. Note: CVE-2026-29092 showed EPG sessions could survive account disable pre-9.2.1, so 'deactivated user loses access' was historically violable in at least one product.
evidence: h2ktrainingvideos.com Kiteworks user-management doc: 'You cannot deactivate a user who is the sole active admin or assigned to scheduled jobs.'; OpenCVE CVE-2026-29092: EPG session management allowed blocked users to maintain active sessions after account disabled (patched 9.2.1).

title: Shared-folder role management is a historically bug-dense surface (CVE-2025-53939)
detail: Prior to 9.1.0, improper input validation when managing roles of a shared folder allowed unexpected elevation of another user's permissions on the share. This confirms the folder role/ownership management code path has produced real priv-esc bugs. The hunting env runs 9.5.1+ (per Kiteworks, all known vulns fixed), so the value is in adjacent/variant logic: role-id handling in /rest/folders/{id} member APIs, downgrade-then-upgrade transitions, stale role caching.
evidence: OpenCVE CVE-2025-53939: 'improper input validation when managing roles of a shared folder could lead to unexpectedly elevate another user's permissions on the share... patched in version 9.1.0'; old Accellion REST API used numeric roleId (downloader=2) via /rest/folders/{id}

title: Mailbox model: sent objects are copies; sender deletion does not revoke recipient access
detail: In the Kiteworks mailbox/send flow, deleting a sent message does NOT delete it for the recipient, and mailbox files auto-expire (30 days in the SEC deployment). Ownership of a 'sent' file is therefore effectively duplicated at send time — revocation after send is impossible by design for that copy. Contrast with shared-folder revocation, which is immediate. Hypothesis agents: probe the boundary between 'sent copy' and 'shared reference' semantics.
evidence: SEC Kiteworks user guide (sec.gov/files/kiteworksguide_0.pdf): 'If you delete a sent message, it will not delete the message for the recipient.'; '30 days after receipt of the message to download the files before they are removed'

title: Open ownership questions for experiment designers
detail: Unresolved from docs alone: (1) Can a folder's OWNERSHIP itself be transferred user-to-user, or only via admin delete-reassignment wizard? (2) When an owner is deactivated (not deleted), do their active shares keep working for recipients? (3) Can a Manager promote themselves to Owner, or demote the Owner? (4) What happens to 'Shared with me' entries when the sharer's account is deleted without reassignment? These are the highest-value manual-test questions on the ownership surface.
evidence: Gap analysis across Getting Started Guide, license-recycling brief, and security overview — none document owner-transfer or deactivated-owner share semantics

title: MFT automated file IMPORT: Airflow-powered scheduled workflows
detail: Kiteworks MFT uses an Apache Airflow-powered graphical workflow designer for automated file movement. Workflows trigger on schedule, polling, events, or manually, and auto-resume failed transfers (even 16TB files). This is the primary machine-driven data IMPORT engine: files flow in from trading partners automatically with no human review per transfer.
evidence: kiteworks.com/managed-file-transfer-solution/: 'Workflows are built and scheduled through the Apache Airflow-powered designer, meaning complex, multi-step automation runs reliably at 5 a.m.'; 'Trigger file transfers with scheduling, polling, or events, or start them manually.'

title: MFT IMPORT sources: ~2000 connectors across SFTP/FTPS/SMB/CIFS/AS2 and cloud stores
detail: Automated import sources include partner SFTP servers (auto transfer in/out at scale), FTPS, SMB/CIFS file shares, AS2, plus AWS S3, Azure Blob/Files, SharePoint, OneDrive, Google Drive, Google Cloud Storage, Box, Wasabi, Dropbox. Library of ~2,000 connectors and workflow functions; declarative custom operators are supported (custom code surface inside workflow authoring).
evidence: kiteworks.com MFT pages: 'SFTP, FTPS, SMB, CIFS, and AS2'; 'AWS S3, Azure Blob, Azure Files, SharePoint, OneDrive, Google Drive, Google Cloud Storage, Box, and Wasabi'; '2,000 connectors and workflow functions'; 'declarative custom operators'

title: MFT automated file EXPORT to same destination set, on schedule
detail: The same workflow engine pushes data OUT to all listed destinations on schedule or event. Export is machine-driven: once a workflow is authored, sensitive files (payroll, PHI, PII per vendor examples) leave the appliance automatically. Authoring is gated by role-based controls over author capabilities and data access per vendor brochure.
evidence: kiteworks.com: 'Kiteworks secure MFT can automatically transfer content in and out of your business partners SFTP servers at scale, with scheduling'; MFT brochure: 'Manage multiple authors and set rolebased controls over their capabilities and data access'

title: User IMPORT: LDAP/AD sync, SCIM provisioning, admin API bulk user endpoints
detail: User data enters via LDAP/AD integration (covered in admin training), SCIM support for identity management (Integration Suite), and admin REST API endpoints for list/add/update/delete users, install users, admin roles, and LDAP groups (documented at /rest/index.html). Deployment checklist references 'Migration, Bulk or Assistant' tooling for bulk onboarding.
evidence: SoftwareOne Integration Suite listing: 'SCIM support for identity management'; Kiteworks admin guide excerpt: '/admin/users endpoints: List, add, update, delete users... LDAP Groups: List, create or delete LDAP groups'; deployment checklist: 'Migration, Bulk or Assistant'

title: Audit log EXPORT: admin report generation and export for compliance
detail: Trusted Audit Logs convert to human-readable forms: administrative reporting of all activities (filterable/searchable), report generation and EXPORT for use in compliance audits, automated compliance reporting, and export to SIEM/syslog (Splunk App, CISO Dashboard drill-down). Data leaves the appliance as generated reports and syslog streams.
evidence: Kiteworks Packaging/Licensing 8.0 PDF: 'Report generation and export for use in compliance audits'; kiteworks.com/platform/advanced-governance/: 'exportable to your syslog and SIEM'; MFT innovations page: 'automated compliance reporting'

title: End-user EXPORT: per-object exportable audit trails and large downloads
detail: End users can export audit data: sent-email Track button yields an exportable timestamped audit trail (who opened/viewed/downloaded attachments); shared-folder Details tab (Owner/Manager/Collaborator) yields an exportable timestamped log of views, downloads, uploads, changes, renames, and invitation/permission changes. File downloads up to 16TB supported.
evidence: Packaging PDF: 'A detailed report gives them an exportable audit trail including timestamps'; 'an exportable, timestamped log of every user who viewed, downloaded, uploaded, changed, or renamed any file'; EPG brief: 'compliant file transfers up to 16 TB'

title: Legal Hold / eDiscovery EXPORT: preserved content with detailed reporting
detail: Advanced Governance add-on preserves all third-party content communications (files, versions, emails, activity traces) for litigation with a provable chain of custody, plus detailed reporting and integrations with email archiving and eDiscovery systems. This is a bulk EXPORT path for sensitive content out of the appliance.
evidence: kiteworks.com/platform/advanced-governance/: 'preservation of all third-party content communications for litigation: files, versions, emails, and activity traces'; 'integrations with email archiving and eDiscovery'

title: Email flows: EPG inbound/outbound monitoring with policy-driven encryption
detail: The Email Protection Gateway sees ALL inbound and outbound email (not just sensitive sent messages), enforcing policies centrally: automated encryption plus expiration/forwarding/view/download/domain controls. Inbound mail is a data import channel; outbound is a data export channel; both are policy-gated.
evidence: EPG feature brief: 'it sees all the outbound and inbound emails'; 'policydriven Email Protection Gateway (EPG) automates encryption'; 'control content with policies for expiration, forwarding, viewing, download access, and domains'

title: Secure Web Forms: structured data IMPORT channel
detail: Secure Web Forms (SDF/Advanced Forms) provide secure data collection - form submissions are a structured data import path into the platform, alongside file upload (web, Outlook plugin, mobile, desktop clients) and the SFTP client (remote SFTP server surfaced as web folders). Submission export format not confirmed from public docs.
evidence: PDN capability lists: 'Secure Web Forms: Secure data collection and handling'; SFTP page: 'The remote SFTP server appears as a set of web folders your end users access'

title: Scheduled/automated EXPORT triggers: compliance reports, alerts, SIEM forwarding
detail: Exports run on schedules without human initiation: automated compliance reporting, admin-configured alerts ('Generate reports and setup alerts' per admin training), syslog/SIEM forwarding of audit activity, and scheduled MFT workflows. DLP/ATP scan results also feed reporting and CISO Dashboard exports.
evidence: MFT innovations page: 'automated compliance reporting'; admin training: 'Generate reports and setup alerts'; advanced-governance: 'All activity is fully logged and visible via reporting and the CISO Dashboard, and exportable to your syslog and SIEM'

Do not burn more requests on it until it responds.
